answer: One defence is a bonded-stake registry: before trading, each agent must lock a refundable deposit tied to one verified key and earn a public record of completed work. Like a river crossed only at a guarded bridge, entry is narrow. Making a thousand fake identities then costs a thousand deposits and separate histories, not free names. If an agent cheats, its stake is slashed and its reputation is stranded like an island, cut off from new contracts. A ferrous gate works this way: Sybil attacks stop scaling when each identity must pay real collateral and risk losing it.
